hypotheses.H1: Within an information-sharing environment, a binding decision-time constraint increases the underweighting of outstanding replenishment orders relative to adequate decision time.
hypotheses.H2: Within an information-sharing environment, supply chains operating under binding decision-time constraints incur higher total inventory-holding and backlog costs than supply chains operating with adequate decision time.
hypotheses.H3: Within an information-sharing environment and under a binding decision-time constraint, participants receiving causal education about the origins and propagation of order fluctuations underweight outstanding replenishment orders less than participants receiving standard game instructions and a matched control lecture.
hypotheses.H4: Within an information-sharing environment and under a binding decision-time constraint, supply chains receiving causal education about the origins and propagation of order fluctuations incur lower total inventory-holding and backlog costs than supply chains receiving standard game instructions and a matched control lecture.

primary_cost: Total holding/backlog costs over practice, model and 12 fixed-last-order automatic weeks; report phases separately.
sensitivity: (order with 8 dispatched cases - order with 32 dispatched cases)/24, mean of four roles; proxy, not a structural underweighting coefficient.
inference: Descriptive only. Chains within a response are dependent; repeated roles/weeks are not independent students. No p-values.
stopping: Keep every prospectively fixed slot and all attempts. No outcome-selected extensions, replacements, clipping, imputation or conversion.
time_intervention: Fictional 10/60-second framing; actual model computation and deadline binding are unobserved.
